summary: The Independent article by Amber Raiken asks whether you should introduce a new partner to your family over the holidays, drawing on two marriage and family therapists. They advise discussing intentions, family dynamics and sleeping arrangements beforehand, checking in with your partner during visits, and not oversharing in advance. They agree there is no universally right or wrong time for the introduction.
one_line: Therapists Rachel Zar and Saba Lurie advise on introducing a partner to your family at the holidays: communicate intentions and family dynamics beforehand, and check in during visits.
key_facts: An American Psychological Association poll found 41 per cent of US adults said their stress levels increased from November to January compared with other months.
Nearly 50 per cent of Americans described their stress level during the holiday season as "moderate".
Rachel Zar, a licensed marriage and family therapist at Spark Chicago Therapy, says expectations are very high during the holidays, so people forget the season comes with a lot of stress.
Saba Lurie, a licensed marriage and family therapist at Take Root Thereapy in California, says there isn't a right or wrong time to introduce a partner but the intentions must be clear.
Lurie advises telling your partner why you are bringing them home so you are on the same page about intentions, and making them aware of any tension or stress in your family.
Zar advises telling relatives if something about your partner could be surprising or differs notably from someone you've brought home before.
Zar advised against oversharing information before Christmas, so family and partner connect in person rather than through the grapevine.
Sleeping arrangements should be discussed ahead of time; Lurie notes that if your family isn't comfortable with you sharing a bedroom with your partner, you may stay elsewhere.
Lurie recommends checking in with your partner during family time, for example asking "How are we doing?" like a temperature check, or going on a walk to reset.
Lurie calls introducing a partner to family "a really vulnerable act" that allows for greater intimacy, since the partner may see another side of you.
Zar says you can explain complex family relationships to your partner, such as a distant brother or your chosen family, showing you have been introspective.
Lurie says "I don't think there's ever going to be a perfect time for folks" and the timing depends on the relationship and family dynamics.
